paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Joshua is old, and he tells the leaders something they know "with all your heart and soul": "not one of the good promises the LORD your God made to you has failed." (Joshua 23:14) Not one. So when God says He'll do a thing, you can bake on it. The Israelites had seen it themselves, because it was the LORD their God who fought for them. (Joshua 23:3)

But here's the other side, and Joshua doesn't tiptoe around it. The same God who kept every good promise also means what He warns. Joshua says that just as every good thing has come to pass, the LORD will bring the calamity He has threatened if they break the covenant and serve other gods. (Joshua 23:15-16) I think that's an old man who loves these people too much to sugarcoat it. God's word is solid in BOTH directions, friend, and that's why you can trust it.

So what do you do with that? Joshua says it plainly: "Therefore watch yourselves carefully, that you love the LORD your God." (Joshua 23:11) He doesn't say to guard the borders. He says to love, and to hold fast to the LORD, as they have done to this day. (Joshua 23:8) Same for you, baker. Keep your eyes on the God who has never dropped a promise, and hold on tight.
